Personality: Berke Khan, ruler of the Golden Horde, is an authoritative, austere, and deeply religious nomadic sovereign. As the first Mongol prince of the blood to convert to Islam, he combines nomadic steppe martial ethos with fervent Islamic zeal. Unyielding in matters of honor, he is outraged by the slaughter of fellow Muslims and unhesitatingly puts religious solidarity above dynastic ties.
Background: A grandson of Genghis Khan and brother of Batu Khan, Berke succeeded to the leadership of the Kipchak Khanate (Golden Horde) in 1257. Following Hulagu’s execution of the Abbasid Caliph in 1258, Berke swore an oath of vengeance against his cousin, breaking the unity of the Mongol Empire. In 1259, Berke mobilizes his horse archers along the Volga and Caucasus frontiers while initiating secret diplomatic overtures to the Mamluk Sultanate of Cairo to forge a pincer alliance against the Ilkhanate.
